gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-inscriptional: Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian keeps wide, open eyes in its letters. Quilon up top carries a faint pen-like modulation in its bowls, while the body underneath is low in contrast and packs a deep middle band.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-jp: Noto Sans JP reads modern and businesslike, with curves that sweep open instead of curling shut and a very high x-height. And Quilon brings editorial command up top, its strokes swelling and thinning above the body's low contrast.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Quilon's stroke weight rises and falls in a slow ebb and flow, giving the display letters an editorial, commanding look. Noto Sans Kayah Li lifts its brush ends away before each curve closes.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-kharoshthi: Quilon leads with mild stress that leaves every stroke solid and readable, display letters with a commanding edge. Noto Sans Kharoshthi does the opposite job, running a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through each line.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Editorial and commanding, Quilon is a display face that runs a lightly shaded texture through every word. Noto Sans Khojki gives every e a large, clear eye and wide exits.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-kr: Quilon brings hairlines that stay fairly sturdy beside its stems, a display face with editorial weight. Noto Sans KR loosens things with stubby ascenders and descenders and generous gaps in its curves.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-lao-looped: Quilon is stencil-cut, with bar widths that vary only mildly. Noto Sans Lao Looped makes paragraphs settle into solid blocks rather than skylines, with bowls left unfinished on one side.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Noto Sans Lepcha reads approachable, its curves keeping a wide opening. Quilon sits up top with weight changes that are present but never dramatic, while the lowercase below has the stature of cast iron capitals.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Noto Sans Limbu has gaping curves and small letters with lofty bodies, an approachable face. Yet Quilon's hairline-free thin strokes beside moderately weighty stems are what make the duo stand out.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Approachable, Noto Sans Lydian keeps capitals barely taller than lowercase. Quilon adds middle-ground stroke contrast and editorial command, a lively foil for a body whose openings stretch like a sprung paper clip.
